Approach: stop modeling more of bash; when the command text contains Git followed by commit or push anywhere (the hook if rule), deny as unclear any construct the scanner does not fully read: a decoded NUL in an ANSI-C word (or cut at it as bash does), an unquoted heredoc whose body holds $( or a backtick, any << that is not followed by a delimiter-shaped word or sits in any arithmetic context ($[ ], (( )) anywhere, C-style for), backslash-newline inside double quotes (drop it as bash does), command substitution inside skipped arithmetic, nested backticks, eval, sh/bash/zsh/fish reading from a pipe, heredoc or -c with non-literal text, wrappers not in the known list (setsid, stdbuf, ionice, flock, find -exec, ssh, env -S), a dynamic Git subcommand (git $p), git -c alias.*, -c remote.*.push, --config-env and --attr-source. The deny reason tells the root to write the command plainly. Keep plain everyday commands (git status, git log, a gh pr create with a quoted heredoc body that has no substitution, plain git push) passing, with tests.

Commit-msg (non-blocking, ride along): only honour a scissors line that git itself would add (the exact line with the configured comment string) and still check for attribution trailers below it; ignore core.commentString coming only from GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS if simple, else document it.

What now gives `unclear` (deny, with the reason telling the root to write the command plainly):
- **B1:** a decoded NUL in a `$'…'` word.
- **B2:** an unquoted heredoc whose body holds `$(` or a backtick. A quoted or backslash-quoted delimiter is plain text and passes.
- **B3:**
  - a `<<` with no delimiter-shaped word after it, or a heredoc whose terminator never comes;
  - `$[ … ]`, also inside double quotes;
  - `(( … ))` anywhere (after `if`/`while`, in `for ((…))`), skipped only when it is plain arithmetic: a `;` (C-style `for`), a quote, a backslash, a newline, no closing `))`, or a substitution in it is unclear. Text after such an arithmetic skip is still scanned, so `if ((1<<2)); then …` followed by a force push is read as a force push.
- **B4:** a backslash-newline inside double quotes is dropped as bash does, so `git "com\<newline>mit"` is read as `git commit`.
- **B5:** a command substitution inside skipped arithmetic.
- Nested backticks; `eval`.
- `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `ash`, `fish`, `csh` and `tcsh` reading a pipe, a heredoc or `-s`, or `-c` with a non-literal script. A literal `-c` script is read; a script file (`bash install/x.sh`) passes.
- Runners it does not follow: `setsid`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `flock`, `ssh`, `su`, `runuser`, `chroot`, `script`, `watch`, `parallel`, `unbuffer`, `taskset`, `chrt`, `numactl`, `eatmydata`, `strace`, `ltrace`, `nsenter`, `unshare`, `systemd-run`, `busybox`, `caffeinate`, `env -S`, and `find -exec|-execdir|-ok|-okdir`.
- A program or git subcommand named by a variable (`$g commit`, `git $p`), and `GIT_CONFIG*` / `GIT_ALIAS*` variables.
- `git -c alias.*`, `-c remote.*.push`, `-c remote.*.mirror`, `-c push.*`, `--config-env` and `--attr-source`.

A word with a variable in it now carries an internal marker, so `bash -c 'echo $HOME'` (single-quoted, literal) passes while `bash -c "echo $HOME"` (expanded by the outer shell) is unclear.

Passing, with tests: `git status`, `git log`, `git show`, plain `git push` (with and without `-u`/`-C`), `gh pr create --body-file - <<'EOF'` with a quoted body that holds `$(…)` text, `gh pr checks --watch`, `gh pr view --json`, branch/merge/stash commands, `bash script.sh`, `bash -c 'literal'`, `find … | xargs grep`, `$((1 + 2))`, a `for` loop, a plain unquoted heredoc and a `mise run verify | tail`.

`commit-msg` (non-blocking items):
- The comment string is read with `git config --show-origin`; a value that comes only from the command line (`-c` or `GIT_CONFIG_*`) is ignored, so it cannot hide text.
- The scissors line is still the exact line with the configured comment string; the phrase check stays above it.
- Attribution lines are now removed from below it as well. A hand-made message keeps everything below such a line.
- Fixed along the way: an unset `core.commentString` no longer hides `core.commentChar` (an empty string had short-circuited the fallback).

Documented limits in `docs/hooks.md`: aliases defined in the user's own git configuration (`git ci`, `git pf`) and scripts that run git inside still escape, and the host's multi-line `if` glob match is still unprobed.
